FN-QUMH415-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 373
Committee: Education Policy Sponsor: Representative Kelvin Lawrence
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 04/01/2024
House Bill 373 as introduced would increase the administrative obligations of the State Board
of Education to establish the new Workforce Pathways diploma at the K-12 level.
Additionally, this bill would increase the administrative and financial obligations of the State
Board of Education, the State Department of Education, and the local boards of education by an
undetermined amount to develop and implement the Workforce Pathways curriculum for K-12
students pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
Further, this bill provides that any increased obligations may be offset in whole or in part by
additional funding by the Legislature to construct, retrofit, or upgrade career and technical
education centers in the state.
Finally, this bill would provide that the Legislature may provide funding for the existing
Alabama Short-Term Credential Program. The Governor's Recommended Fiscal Year 2025
appropriation includes $1 million for this program under the Alabama Community College
System.

FN-QUMH415-2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 373
Committee: Education Policy Sponsor: Representative Kelvin Lawrence
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 04/10/2024
House Bill 373 as reported by the Committee on Education Policy would increase the
administrative obligations of the State Department of Education to: (1) conduct a
comprehensive review of the state's graduation requirements and coordinate their review with
stakeholder within the state; (2) before November 1, 2024, propose a comprehensive set of
gradation requirements that include multiple pathways for a high school diploma; and (3) collect
information and publish a report annually on the pathways a student may use to earn a high
school diploma.
Further, this bill provides that any increased obligations may be offset in whole or in part by
additional funding by the Legislature to construct, retrofit, or upgrade career and technical
education centers in the state.
Finally, this bill would provide that the Legislature may provide funding for the existing
Alabama Short-Term Credential Program. The Governor's Recommended Fiscal Year 2025
appropriation includes $1 million for this program under the Alabama Community College
System.
